title: `with sharing`, `without sharing`, inherited sharing, and user/system execution context
objectives: Choose with sharing, without sharing, or inherited sharing and explain the API 67.0 default.
State that sharing keywords do not enforce object or field permissions.
Separate record-sharing mode from user-mode versus system-mode database operations.
Refuse without sharing except as a documented, targeted elevation.
diagnostic_question: A community user must read a LAB_ FAQ article they do not own. A service class is also called from a with-sharing controller and from a batch job. Which sharing keyword, and does that enforce FLS?
definition: Apex sharing keywords choose whether the current user's sharing rules are enforced: with sharing enforces them, without sharing does not, and inherited sharing uses the caller's mode. In API version 67.0 and later, a class without an explicit sharing declaration runs in with sharing mode. Sharing keywords do not enforce object or field permissions. User mode versus system mode is the separate CRUD/FLS execution context. ([Sharing Keywords](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_keywords_sharing.htm); [Enforce Sharing](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_security_sharing_rules.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail candidates who say with sharing equals FLS, or who mark every class without sharing 'so queries work.' API 67.0 changed the implicit default to with sharing. Inherited sharing is how a service class stays honest when callers differ.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a museum after hours. With sharing means the visitor escort rules apply: you only enter galleries your ticket already allows. Without sharing is a documented master key for one job, such as letting an Experience Cloud user read a knowledge article they could not otherwise reach. Inherited sharing means the service cart uses whoever wheeled it in. Checking tickets at the door (CRUD/FLS) is user mode—a different lock than the escort rules.
deeper_explanation: Use with sharing or without sharing to specify whether sharing rules are enforced. Use inherited sharing to run in the sharing mode of the calling class. The documented default sharing mode is with sharing. Salesforce recommends declaring the keyword explicitly. ([Sharing Keywords](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_keywords_sharing.htm))

In API 67.0 and later, classes without an explicit sharing declaration run in with sharing mode. In API 66.0 and earlier, implicit behavior depended on inheritance, Aura/@AuraEnabled entry, and caller mode. Do not quote the old implicit without-sharing story for a 67.0 class. ([Sharing Keywords](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_keywords_sharing.htm))

Using with sharing does not enforce the user's object permissions and field-level security. Sharing rules are distinct from, and can coexist with, object-level and field-level permissions. ([Enforce Sharing](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_security_sharing_rules.htm))

Without sharing is for targeted elevation, for example allowing community users to read records they would not otherwise access. Use it with caution so you do not expose data hidden by sharing. Inherited sharing is for service classes that must support both modes. An inherited-sharing class runs as without sharing only when explicitly called from an already established without-sharing context. ([Sharing Keywords](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_classes_keywords_sharing.htm))

The LWC Developer Guide states that in API 67.0 and later, Apex runs in user mode by default, meaning current-user object permissions and FLS are enforced unless a database operation is explicitly set to system mode. Sharing keywords remain the record-level control. ([Secure Apex Classes](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/apex-security.html))

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Sharing keywords choose record visibility in Apex. API 67 defaults to with sharing. without sharing is targeted elevation. inherited sharing follows the caller. None of those keywords enforce FLS; user mode does.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I read the class API version first. On 67 I treat omitted keywords as with sharing, but I still declare them. I pick inherited sharing for services. I use without sharing only with a written reason, such as a community user reading a specified object. I separately say user mode is the CRUD/FLS default on 67 and that with sharing will not hide Amount. I mention the Pricebook2 exception so I do not over-claim.

terminology.plain: Apex honors the running user's record sharing.
terminology.precise: Declare the class so sharing rules of the current user are enforced. Recommended default.
terminology.non_example: Assuming with sharing also hides Amount.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: User mode: object and field permissions.

terminology.plain: Apex ignores the running user's sharing rules.
terminology.precise: Targeted elevation. The guide's example includes community users reading records they would not otherwise access.
terminology.example: A narrow LAB_FaqReader without sharing for published FAQ rows.
terminology.non_example: Putting without sharing on every class so tests pass.

terminology.plain: Use whatever sharing mode the caller already has.
terminology.precise: Runs with sharing unless explicitly called from an established without-sharing context. Good for service classes.
terminology.non_example: Omitting the keyword and calling that inherited on API 67—omission is with sharing.
terminology.boundary: Declare it so intent is obvious.

terminology.plain: Database work respects the user's object and field permissions.
terminology.precise: API 67 default for Apex: permissions and FLS enforced unless an operation is set to system mode.
terminology.example: A query that fails when LAB_Rep lacks Amount FLS.
terminology.boundary: Confirm AccessLevel syntax in current DML docs.

terminology.plain: A database operation that ignores the user's object and field permissions.
terminology.precise: Must be explicit in API 67+. Sharing keywords are a different switch.
terminology.example: A documented system-mode operation in a privileged service—Needs verification of the exact API you will type.
terminology.non_example: without sharing, which is record sharing, not FLS.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent method names in the interview if you have not re-read them.

terminology.plain: Omitted sharing keyword means with sharing.
terminology.precise: Versioned behavior: 67+ implicit with sharing; 66 and earlier used a multi-factor implicit rule.

interview_questions.question: Explain with sharing, without sharing, and inherited sharing.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: with sharing enforces the user's sharing. without sharing does not, and is a targeted elevation. inherited sharing follows the caller and is without sharing only if the caller already is.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I add the API 67 default: omitted keywords run with sharing, but I still declare them. I pick inherited for services. I use without sharing only with a written community or batch reason. I immediately say none of this is FLS. That sequence is the interview-ready answer.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CaseService inherited sharing; LAB_FaqReader without sharing for published FAQs; LAB_CaseReader with sharing for the LWC.
tradeoffs: Explicit keywords vs relying on defaults

interview_questions.question: What changed for implicit sharing in API 67.0?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Classes without an explicit sharing declaration run in with sharing mode. Older API 66 behavior used a multi-factor implicit rule and must not be taught as current for 67 classes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I read the class version before I answer. On 67 I treat omission as with sharing. On 66 I say implicit mode depended on inheritance, Aura entry, and caller, and I would re-read the table rather than recite unofficial lore. I recommend declaring the keyword so a version bump does not surprise you.
interview_questions.example: A helper saved as 67.0 with no keyword still enforces sharing for LAB_Rep.
tradeoffs: Upgrading API versions vs silent sharing changes
weak_answer_warnings: Teaching 66 implicit without sharing as the 67 default

interview_questions.question: An LWC must show only Cases the user can see, and Amount must honor FLS. Design the Apex class.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Declare with sharing for record visibility. Rely on user-mode database operations for FLS, not on the sharing keyword. Test as LAB_Rep, not as admin.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I put with sharing on the controller even though API 67 defaults to it. I do not use without sharing to make the list look full. I state that with sharing will not hide Amount. If Amount still appears, I inspect user mode versus an explicit system-mode operation. I keep restriction rules and OWD out of the Apex keyword answer unless asked.
interview_questions.example: public with sharing class LAB_CaseLwc on API 67.0 querying Cases for the current user.
tradeoffs: User-mode failures vs privileged system mode
with sharing vs inherited on a shared service
follow_ups: When would you use inherited sharing instead?
weak_answer_warnings: with sharing as the FLS answer

interview_questions.question: A batch job must update Cases the running user cannot see. How do you avoid a without-sharing culture?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I isolate elevation in a small without-sharing or established privileged caller, keep user-facing classes with sharing, and use inherited sharing on the service so it follows each caller.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not stamp without sharing on the LWC controller. I write the elevation reason next to the privileged class. I test both callers. I still separate CRUD/FLS: a batch may need system mode, which is not the same keyword. I mention security review and least privilege. I would not change OWD to make the batch easier.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CaseNightly without sharing calls LAB_CaseService inherited sharing; the LWC controller stays with sharing.
tradeoffs: One privileged class vs spreading without sharing
follow_ups: How do you test both callers?
What does inherited do if the batch is without sharing?

interview_questions.question: Why is inherited sharing better than omitting the keyword?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: On API 67 omission means with sharing, not inherited. inherited sharing is an explicit, reviewable choice that a service can run either way.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The guide calls inherited sharing an advanced technique to decide mode at run time. Omitting the keyword used to look like 'inherit from caller' in older mental models and in some 66 paths. That ambiguity is why security reviews want the word inherited on the page. I declare it on helpers and I still test both callers.
interview_questions.example: public inherited sharing class LAB_CaseService used by both the LWC and the nightly job.
tradeoffs: Clarity vs slightly more verbose headers
Flexible services vs surprising without-sharing callers
follow_ups: When does inherited become without sharing?

interview_questions.question: Apex returns a Case the user cannot open in the UI. Walk the diagnosis.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I inspect the class sharing keyword, the caller chain, the API version, and whether I am running as that user. A without-sharing helper is the usual leak.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: UI uses sharing plus CRUD/FLS. Apex can bypass sharing if a class is without sharing or called that way. I read headers down the stack. I check API 67 defaults so I do not misread an omitted keyword. If the user also should not see Amount, I switch to the user-mode conversation. I do not 'fix' it by opening OWD.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CaseLwc with sharing called LAB_CaseUtil without sharing; the util query leaked the peer Case.
tradeoffs: Fixing the helper vs widening UI sharing
Keeping a privileged util vs splitting APIs

interview_questions.question: How do you talk about user mode and sharing keywords in one minute without mixing them?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Sharing keywords choose record rows. User mode versus system mode chooses object and field permissions. API 67 defaults both toward the running user. They are two locks.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw two columns. Left: with, without, inherited. Right: user mode, system mode. I say with sharing will not hide Amount, and user mode will not invent a sharing path. I mention you can still have a with-sharing class perform a system-mode operation if someone coded that—so I read the operation, not only the class header. I refuse to invent AccessLevel method names if I have not just read them.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CaseReader with sharing still returns Amount if a system-mode query is used and FLS would have hidden it.
tradeoffs: Honesty about syntax vs bluffing APIs
follow_ups: Does inherited sharing change user mode?
weak_answer_warnings: One keyword to rule them all

interview_questions.question: Teach the museum-escort analogy, then break it with Pricebook2 and a caller chain.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Escort rules are sharing keywords; ticket checks are user mode; the master key is without sharing. It breaks because Pricebook2 ignores the escort, and a with-sharing room can still call a master-key helper.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk LAB_Rep through the museum. I show inherited sharing as using whoever wheeled the cart. I then open the Pricebook2 exception and the with-calls-without warning so I do not sound like a brochure. I finish with API 67: if you forget to label the door, the escort still applies, which is safer than the old stories and still not an excuse to skip the keyword.
interview_questions.example: LAB_CaseReader with sharing calls LAB_CaseUtil without sharing and also queries Pricebook2.
follow_ups: What is the community-user elevation example?
